notes: National government scheme of the Government of the Czech Republic (Ministry of Education, Youth and Sports / Dum zahraniční spoluprace), implemented under the Czech foreign development cooperation programme. Scholarships fund study at ANY Czech public higher education institution; applicants choose the university/programme, so no single institution or supervising professor is attached to the award. Official page (given URL) currently returns 'Stranka nenalezena' (404); the active official page is https://msmt.gov.cz/en/scholarships/government-scholarships-developing-countries. Research contact for government scholarships is registr@dzs.cz (Czech National Agency for International Education and Research) per the MŠMT Scholarships page.

Institution-wide Charles University scheme: the official page (https://cuni.cz/UKEN-1617.html) states that full-time doctoral students receive a doctoral study income of at least 1.2x the Czech minimum wage for the standard length of doctoral study (4 years), as a doctoral scholarship, creative-work wage, or a combination. The income is university-wide and not tied to any specific department, research group, or professor; supervisors are arranged individually between the student and the chosen faculty. No official Charles University page names a professor tied to this scheme, so no professor entries could be verified.

International Visegrad Fund mobility programme (Visegrad Fellowship Program, Visegrad Scholarship Program, Visegrad-Taiwan Scholarships, etc.). The Fund is a regional funding body, not a university: fellows/scholars choose their own host institution in a V4 (or other eligible) country, so no supervising professor is attached to the award. Official page: https://www.visegradfund.org/scholarships.

Host institution is Masaryk University, Brno, but the official page (https://czs.muni.cz/en/student-from-abroad/other-possibilities/visegrad-grant) only instructs applicants to contact the international office of the specific Masaryk faculty to obtain the letter of acceptance; the Fund awards and funds the scholarship. The Faculty International Offices page (https://czs.muni.cz/en/student-from-abroad/international-student-guide/faculty-international-offices) lists only office contacts (e.g. int@law.muni.cz, int@sci.muni.cz), not named professors or supervisors, and no official page ties any professor to this scholarship.

Central EU Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scholarship listing (European Commission / EACEA). EMJM programmes are consortia of at least three higher education institutions in at least three countries; students apply directly to the programme coordinator, and the Commission country listing pages attach no single institution or supervising professor to the award. (The given country-page URL currently returns 404; the central EMJM students page is https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/erasmus-mundus-joint-masters-scholarships.)

National public funding call by the Portuguese Foundation for Science and Technology (FCT). The official call page (https://www.fct.pt/en/concursos/concurso-bolsas-de-doutoramento-2026-linha-de-candidatura-geral) states that the regular line of application covers all scientific areas and that candidates designate their own contracting/host institution (any Portuguese or foreign HEI, R&D unit, or Associated Laboratory), so no institution or supervising professor is attached to the award. Contact for the call: info.bolsas@fct.pt.

Central EU Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters scholarship listing (European Commission / EACEA). EMJM programmes are transnational consortia (at least three institutions from three countries) whose degrees run 1-2 academic years; students apply to the programme coordinator and the Commission country listing pages attach no single institution or supervising professor to the award. (The given country-page URL currently returns 404; the central EMJM students page is https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/erasmus-mundus-joint-masters-scholarships.)
